source.title: Large language models in judicial assistance: Empirical insights and domain-specific fine-tuning
source.authors: Su Zhu; Jiahui Zhao; Yu-Nan Chen; Xu Sun; Xi Zheng

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses weakly supervised fine-tuning as a method for judicial tasks and reports its performance, but it does not compare the fine-tuned student with the model that produced the weak labels or calculate PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper generates weakly labeled legal Q&A data and fine-tunes Baichuan with LoRA. It compares results with the base Baichuan model and GPT-4o, not with an identified weak supervisor. It reports no PGR, so these results do not test whether the student beats its weak labeler. Reported results from the 13-model benchmark are not included because they do not apply the weak-label fine-tuning intervention. No cited result is counted.
record.test_reason: The study trains Baichuan-7B with LoRA on 9,605 model-generated 'weakly labeled' Q&A pairs. The pairs come from an unnamed model fine-tuned on 500 hand-labeled pairs and are filtered by GPT-3.5. Results are compared only with base Baichuan and GPT-4o. The model that produced the labels is never evaluated, its size relative to the student is not stated, and there is no strong ceiling or PGR. So no result bears on whether a student beats its weak supervisor. This is classic weak or pseudo-label supervision used as a tool, not a weak-to-strong test. T6 would also be defensible, since the paper never invokes the weak-to-strong finding.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that weakly supervised domain fine-tuning substantially improves Baichuan on judicial tasks, especially structured extraction and decision generation. Legal opinion generation remains below GPT-4o.
record.recipe_differences: The study generates weakly labeled legal Q&A pairs through a multi-stage process and fine-tunes Baichuan with LoRA; it does not use the original study's weak-to-strong setup or PGR measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured outcomes differ across the five judicial tasks; legal opinion generation improves less and remains below GPT-4o.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA fine-tuning of Baichuan-7B on filtered model-generated legal Q&A raises F1 over base Baichuan on all five tasks. Examples: average extraction 0.23 to 0.69, judicial decision 0.306 to 0.811, legal opinion 0.389 to 0.467. It exceeds GPT-4o on most tasks but not on legal opinion generation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on filtered, model-generated domain labels improves a model over its base checkpoint, with gains varying by task.

record.problems: The weak-labeling model is not clearly identified as a supervisor whose performance can be compared with the student. The paper provides no PGR or uncertainty estimates for the fine-tuning benchmark results. The fine-tuned model is evaluated against its base checkpoint and GPT-4o, not the weak labeler.
record.rows_left_out: No weak-label training results were left out. The 13-model benchmark results in Tables 2–6 and the human-evaluation results are omitted because they do not report outcomes of the weak-label fine-tuning intervention.

untested.parts: No weak-supervisor score, no strong ceiling and no PGR. The labeling model (Model 2) is unnamed and never evaluated.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling or loss variants compared against naive fine-tuning.
No variation in supervisor or student size. Task differences are reported only relative to base Baichuan and GPT-4o, not as PGR.
No distribution-shift, supervisor-checkability or error-overlap analysis.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. GPT-4o is a reference model, not the supervisor; GPT-3.5 only filters the generated labels. The labeling model is described only as 'the large model' fine-tuned on 500 pairs, so the supervisor could even be Baichuan itself, which would make this self-training. The paper states 1,921 weakly labeled cases in Section 3.1 but 9,605 Q&A pairs elsewhere; these are consistent (1,921 × 5). The record's uncertainty_reported 'y' applies only to the human-evaluation confidence intervals; the fine-tuning results have no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison with the weak supervisor and no PGR calculation.
No comparison of auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling, loss variants, or PGR against naive fine-tuning.
The study reports outcomes across legal tasks, but does not measure PGR or compare its dependence on supervisor/student size, task families, or representations.
No tests of supervisor-checkability, distribution shift, or overlap in supervisor and student errors.
No theoretical conditions for a student beating its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language modality.
